data.one_liner: Performant vector maps for Flutter supporting Mapbox Vector Tiles across all six platforms.
data.what_it_does: Renders interactive vector and raster maps using the MapLibre Native C API and maplibre-gl-js. It provides typed style layers, sources, offline map capabilities, and declarative annotations that render directly into Flutter textures or HTML elements.
use_when: You need interactive vector or raster maps across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and web.
You want maps to render into Flutter textures so that standard widgets compose seamlessly over and around them.
avoid_when: You require the older maplibre_gl package architecture and are not ready to migrate to version 0.4.
Your project targets Android versions below API level 24, iOS 15, or macOS 14.3.
strengths: Supports six platforms using a unified API via FFI and JS interop.
Fast interop without platform views on desktop and mobile.
Full style spec with typed style layers, sources, and expressions.
weaknesses: UI widgets like map compass do not automatically follow the app's Material Theme.
Requires minimum OS versions (Android API 24, iOS 15, macOS 14.3).
data.setup_notes: Requires platform setup steps and specific minimum OS versions (Android API 24, iOS 15, macOS 14.3). Swift Package Manager is required for iOS and macOS.

alternatives.name: flutter_map
alternatives.why_pick_it: A pure Dart interactive map package that does not rely on native MapLibre SDKs.

alternatives.name: google_maps_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your application specifically requires Google Maps data and platform views rather than MapLibre.
